# 🤔 Frequently Asked Questions

Below is a list of common questions and issues you may encounter. If you have suggestions, please join the [FAQ Suggestions discussion on the GitHub repository](https://github.com/bmeares/Meerschaum/discussions/46)!

??? faq "How do I upgrade to the latest version?"
    You can install the latest version of Meerschaum with `pip install --upgrade meerschaum` or the command `mrsm upgrade mrsm`, which upgrades the installation `mrsm` runs from (pip, uv, pipx, Cargo or a downloaded binary) where it is installed and, when Docker is available and you use the stack, asks whether to pull the stack's new images and bring it up (`--no-pull` skips the pull). Inside a Docker container, pull the new image and recreate the container instead (see the [migration guide](/reference/migrating-to-v5/#upgrading-an-installation)).

??? faq "`mrsm` doesn't work!"
    You can invoke `mrsm` directly with `python -m meerschaum`. Check that your `PATH` includes scripts installed by `pip`, such as `~/.local/bin`.

    ```
    export PATH=$PATH:~/.local/bin
    ```

??? faq "How do I turn off the emoji and/or colors?"
    The color and emoji configuration settings are contained in the `system` config file under the `formatting` section, which you can access with `edit config system`.

    Alternatively, you can install the `color` plugin which will toggle these values for you. The `color` command will toggle `unicode` and `ansi` settings by default, or you can specify `color unicode` or `color ansi` if you want to toggle specific values.
    ```
    install plugins color
    color
    ```
    Note that disabling ANSI may not completely elimate ANSI characters.

??? faq "Can I use Meerschaum in my scripts?"
    Yes, although some commands like `bootstrap` and `edit` are interactive and not safe for scripting, most commands are scriptable.

    When executing Meerschaum actions in a script, it's a good idea to add `--nopretty` and `--noask` flags, or `--yes` or `--force` to agree to confirmation dialogues.

    The flag `--noask` will choose the default values for questions (e.g. skipping deleting to prevent data loss) and `--yes` of `--force` will choose `yes` to agree to all dialogues.

    The `--nopretty` flag may not have 100% coverage, but in cases like `show pipes` or `show columns`, it will instead print JSON representations of the pipes and data (separated by newlines) rather than formatting them.

    If you are planning on integrating Meerschaum into your Python scripts, you can access actions directly via the `meerschaum.actions.actions` dictionary. Please consult [the Python package documentation](https://docs.meerschaum.io) for more information. Also, you might want to consider making your script into a [Meerschaum action by writing an action plugin](/reference/plugins/types-of-plugins/#action-plugins).

??? faq "Connectors don't work for `<database flavor>`!"
    Pipe operations run through Meerschaum's own Rust drivers, which support these flavors: `timescaledb`, `timescaledb-ha`, `postgresql`, `postgis`, `citus`, `cockroachdb`, `mssql`, `mysql`, `mariadb`, `oracle`, `sqlite`, `geopackage` and `duckdb` (see [Supported Flavors](/reference/connectors/sql-connectors/#supported-flavors)). If your database isn't listed, you might be able to use a supported flavor that speaks the same protocol (e.g. `postgresql` is a commonly shared flavor).

    Most flavors need nothing else installed. Microsoft SQL Server needs no ODBC driver. Two flavors need a client library:

    - **Oracle** needs [Oracle Instant Client](https://www.oracle.com/database/technologies/instant-client.html) (`libclntsh`) on the loader path; see [Oracle SQL](/reference/connectors/sql-connectors/#oracle-sql).
    - **DuckDB** uses the `meerschaum[sql-duckdb]` extra in Python, or downloads DuckDB's own library on first use; see [DuckDB](/reference/connectors/sql-connectors/#duckdb).

    Run `mrsm show drivers` to see whether these libraries were found, and `mrsm doctor` for a full health check.

    Raw SQL from Python (`conn.read()`, `conn.exec()`, `conn.engine`) still goes through SQLAlchemy and needs the `meerschaum[sql]` extra, plus `meerschaum[sql-mssql]` (`pyodbc`, which needs Microsoft's [ODBC driver](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/connect/odbc/linux-mac/installing-the-microsoft-odbc-driver-for-sql-server)) or `meerschaum[sql-oracle]` for those flavors.

??? faq "How do I completely uninstall Meerschaum?"
    - Take down your stack and delete its data with `mrsm stack down -v`.
        - You might also want to delete `bmeares/meerschaum` and other images with `docker image rm`.
    - Uninstall via `pip`: `pip uninstall meerschaum`.
    - Delete the folder `~/.config/meerschaum/` (`%APPDATA%\Meerschaum\` on Windows).


---

# ⬆️ Migrating to v5

Source: https://meerschaum.io/reference/migrating-to-v5/

# ⬆️ Migrating to v5

Meerschaum v5 runs its core, CLI, jobs, Compose, HTTP API, and MCP server in Rust. Your existing tables, YAML configuration, Pipe definitions, and Python plugins stay compatible—check the deliberate changes below before upgrading.

## Upgrade checklist

1. Back up your configuration and database; keep your v4.1 venv for rollback.
2. Confirm **Python 3.11+** (only needed for Python plugins, the Python API, or extras).
3. Install the extras you use (`meerschaum[polars]`, `[pandas]`, `[dash]`, `[api]`, etc.).
4. Test a sync, downstream pipe, and scheduled job on a scratch `MRSM_ROOT_DIR` against a copy of your database.
5. Review [teams and permissions](#teams-access-and-permissions) if you run a shared API server.
6. Upgrade, run `mrsm doctor`, and check `mrsm show jobs` (re-enter any blank legacy command with `mrsm edit jobs NAME`).

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade meerschaum
mrsm doctor
```

See the [v5 changelog](../changelog/v5.md) for new features and [Stack upgrades](stack/upgrades.md) for PostgreSQL maintenance.

## Upgrading an installation

**Python 3.11+ and a zero-dependency wheel.** Python 3.10, `setup.py`, and `pyoxidizer` portable archives are removed. `pip install meerschaum` ships a dependency-free maturin wheel containing the Rust core and Python SDK (`mrsm` and `python -m meerschaum` run the native CLI). For a standalone binary without Python, use `cargo install meerschaum --locked` (Rust 1.95+) or GitHub Releases.

| Extra | Installs | Needed when |
|---|---|---|
| `[polars]` | `polars` | New-root default (`dataframe: polars`) or `as_polars=True`. |
| `[pandas]` | `pandas`, `pyarrow` | Upgraded-root `dataframe: pandas` or `as_pandas=True`. |
| `[geo]` | `shapely`, `pyproj`, `geopandas`, `geoarrow-types` | Python geometry objects or GeoDataFrames. |
| `[sql]` | `SQLAlchemy`, `psycopg`, `PyMySQL` | Explicit `conn.engine` or SQLAlchemy sessions (native SQL needs none). |
| `[sql-mssql]`, `[sql-oracle]`, `[sql-duckdb]`, `[sql-cockroachdb]` | Flavor drivers | Explicit SQLAlchemy access (`[sql-duckdb]` also enables shared Python DuckDB). |
| `[api]` | `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `a2wsgi`, `PyJWT`, `websockets`, `python-multipart` | Plugins using `@api_plugin`, `@web_page`, or Python MCP tools. |
| `[dash]` | `dash`, `dash-bootstrap-components`, `dash-ace`, `dash-extensions`, `[api]`, `pandas` | Web console (`/dash`) or `@dash_plugin` pages. |
| `[shell]` / `[gui]` / `[cli-tools]` | `ptpython` / `pywebview` / `pgcli`, `mycli`, `litecli`, `gadwall` | `mrsm python`, `mrsm start gui`, or Python SQL shells. |
| `[full]` | `pandas`, `polars`, `geo`, `sql`, `api`, `dash`, `shell` | All standard integrations (default Docker image; `:slim` ships base wheel only). |

**Self-upgrades (`mrsm upgrade mrsm`).** Upgrades the owning install (`pip`/`uv`/`pipx`, Cargo, or binary) in place without inferring the target from `MRSM_PYTHON`. Prompts are asked up front (upgrade, stack pull, stack restart; flags: `--yes`, `--noask`, `--force`, `--no-pull`, `-A --pre`, `-A --version X.Y.Z`, and `-A --break-system-packages` on PEP 668 distros).

!!! warning "Upgrading a `--user` install from 5.0.x"
    When `uv` is installed, 5.0.x's `mrsm upgrade mrsm` in a `--user` install tries to write to system site-packages. Upgrade to 5.1.0+ with pip directly:
    ```bash
    python3 -m pip install --user --upgrade meerschaum
    ```

**DuckDB and Oracle drivers.** Python hosts with `meerschaum[sql-duckdb]` and `MRSM_DUCKDB_LIB` unset share the Python DuckDB driver across Rust Pipe operations and SQLAlchemy. Standalone and base installs load `libduckdb` (v1.4+) via [`MRSM_DUCKDB_LIB`](environment.md#mrsm_duckdb_lib), `<root>/drivers/`, system paths, or checksum-verified download (`mrsm install driver duckdb`, `mrsm show drivers`). Oracle now requires Instant Client (`libclntsh`) instead of thin mode.

## Behavior changes at a glance

| Area | v4.1 | v5 |
|---|---|---|
| **YAML & config** | PyYAML tags (`!!python/object`) allowed; truncated writes | Safe native YAML (rejects `!!python/*` except `!!python/tuple`); atomic `0600` writes. `api.uvicorn.*` → `api.server.*`. |
| **Env vars** | Any `MRSM_<X>_<Y>` became a connector; `MRSM_NO_AUTO_INSTALL` still fetched `semver`/`uv` | Only built-in (`sql`, `api`, `valkey`, `plugin`, `systemd`) and `@make_connector` types become connectors. [`MRSM_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1`](environment.md#mrsm_no_auto_install) blocks *all* implicit installs. |
| **Timeouts** | 30 s+ retries on unreachable servers | Fails fast on refused/DNS/auth errors, or after `connect_timeout` / [`MRSM_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`](environment.md#mrsm_connect_timeout) (default `5` s). Raise for serverless DBs. |
| **Python DB errors** | `read`/`exec`/`value` and `pipe.get_data`/`get_rowcount`/`get_sync_time` returned `None`/`0` | Raise DB / `5xx` errors; pass `silent=True` for v4 behavior. Unsynced pipes still read empty. |
| **DataFrames** | Always pandas; `as_dask=True` supported | Fresh roots default to **Polars**; upgraded 4.x roots auto-pin `dataframe: pandas`. Dask removed (`TypeError`—use `as_iterator=True` or `as_polars=True`). |
| **Null-like strings** | `'None'`, `'NA'`, `'nan'`, `''` stored/queried as `NULL` | Literal text in declared text and text index columns (use `None` / `'_None'` for SQL NULL; Oracle `''` stays `NULL`). |
| **Unique keys & `mrsm` pipes** | Duplicate pipe/user/plugin rows allowed; `mrsm` pipes shown | Adds unique indexes `uq_mrsm_pipes_keys`, `uq_mrsm_users_username`, `uq_mrsm_plugins_plugin_name` (`mrsm doctor` flags duplicates). `mrsm` pipes hidden unless `-c mrsm`. |
| **Debug & colors** | `dprint()` to stdout; colors when piped; `--nopretty` exited `0` | [`--debug` / `dprint()`](troubleshooting.md#debug-output) write to **stderr** (secrets redacted). Colors disable when piped (`NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`). `--nopretty` exits `1` on failure. |
| **CLI & editors** | `--engine laps`, CLI daemons, `pyvim` fallback | `--loop` replaces `--engine laps`; CLI daemons retired; editors use `$VISUAL` → `$EDITOR` → `vi`. `mrsm python script.py [args]` runs the script. |
| **Auth & limits** | Open defaults; failed scope reads granted all; no body limit | First user is admin; self-registration off; default role `editor`. Permissions fail closed (`503`). Pre-v5 JWTs/sessions re-login once (API keys stay). Request limits enforced (`api:limits`, `413`). |

## Jobs, CLI, and Compose

- **Every root uses `systemd`.** On systemd hosts, v5 uses `systemd` for *all* roots—including Compose projects (`mrsm-<job>.service`, `mrsm-<project>.<job>.service`, `mrsm-<hash>.<job>.service`), pinning `MRSM_PYTHON`. Existing `local` jobs move on the next `compose up` or `restart jobs`; opt out with `meerschaum:executor: local`.
- **Staggered startup & job health.** Bulk starts stagger via `jobs.startup.*` (`--no-stagger` skips). `--loop` repeats *any* action and tracks laps/health ([Job health](background-jobs/health.md)).
- **Stricter jobs & API redaction.** Job names must be one path component. Remote jobs inherit the server's env (keeping Compose stamps), `GET /jobs` redacts secrets, and console workers are scoped to owner, team managers, and admins.
- **Chains vs Pipelines.** `a + b : <flags>` action chains (and saved 4.1 chain jobs) keep running; `start pipeline NAME` / `stop pipeline NAME` now manage saved Pipelines.
- **Compose & copy.** `mrsm compose explain` is side-effect free (no DBs, caches, or installs) and validates missing references; `compose up` checks job ownership first and forwards `--allow-protected`; `include:` / `parent:` support multi-project trees ([Compose](compose.md)). `copy pipes` exits `1` if any pipe fails, and `--sync-data incremental` syncs only new rows.
- **Interactive UX.** `show data` truncates like pandas (`--all` prints all); `show sizes` counts shared tables once; `show pipes` lists failing pipes; `bootstrap pipes` suggests keys with a new SQL prompt order; Ctrl-C cleanly cancels and releases leases.

## The syncing engine

v5 tracks pipe dependencies (`parents`, `children`, and `{{ Pipe() }}` references) for multi-pipe runs, dry-run plans, and resumable executions:

```bash
mrsm sync pipes -c sql:main -m daily_rollup --parents   # ancestors first
mrsm sync pipes -c sql:main -m raw_events --children    # downstream pipes
mrsm plan pipes -t reports --parents                    # dry run
mrsm sync pipes -t reports --parents --resume <run_id>  # resume failed nodes
mrsm start pipeline daily                               # background Pipeline job
```

Bare `sync pipes` keeps v4 semantics, except every sync records a status row in `mrsm_engine_sync_status` (`pipe.get_sync_status()`, `GET /engine/sync-status`). Inside engine runs (`--parents`, `--children`, `mrsm.Pipeline`, or `--loop` with edges):

- Children never sync past their parents' minimum sync time.
- Editing a pipe's `sql`, `fetch`, `dtypes`, or `columns` triggers a **rebuild** (prompts interactively; in jobs sets `rebuild_pending` without blocking unless `--yes` or `system.engine.auto_rebuild: true`).
- Scheduled children follow parent updates rather than their own timer.

See [Pipelines](pipelines/index.md), [Continuous mode](pipelines/continuous.md), and [Engine state](pipelines/state.md#settings).

## Python library and SQL connectors

Public APIs (`mrsm.Pipe`, `get_connector`, `get_config`, `pipe.sync`, `get_data`, `verify`, `filter_existing`, `enforce_dtypes`) keep their v4 signatures:

- **`mrsm.SyncResult`:** `pipe.sync()` returns a tuple subclass unpacking as `(success, message)` with `inserted`, `updated`, `upserted`, `deleted`, `changed_intervals`, and `duration`. PyArrow Tables/RecordBatches, tuples, and chunk generators all sync natively in Rust.
- **Native SQL:** `SQLConnector.read()`, `exec()`, `exec_queries()`, `value()`, `to_sql()`, and catalog helpers run in Rust without `meerschaum[sql]`. `exec()` returns `NativeResult` (`lastrowid` is `None`; `commit=False` rolls back). Keep `[sql]` for `.engine` or explicit SQLAlchemy transactions (or set `native_sql: false`). Avoid mixing `.engine`/`sqlite3` with native calls on the same SQLite/GeoPackage file.
- **DataFrames & timezones:** Override the DataFrame library with `meerschaum.yaml`'s `dataframe`, `MRSM_DATAFRAME`, or `as_polars`/`as_pandas` ([Reading data](pipes/reading.md#dataframe-library)). Pandas reads return Arrow-backed dtypes (`double[pyarrow]`, `large_string[pyarrow]`, `timestamp[ns, tz=UTC][pyarrow]`); PostgreSQL UTC tzinfo is `datetime.timezone.utc` instead of `ZoneInfo('Etc/UTC')`. Convert frames in pandas-only hooks with `meerschaum.utils.dataframe.to_pandas(df)`.
- **API & Valkey clients:** `APIConnector.make_request()` returns lightweight `ApiResponse` (no `requests` dependency); `ValkeyConnector.client` falls back to a built-in client unless `valkey` is installed.
- **New helpers:** `pipe.sync(..., replace=True)` ([Replacing a window](pipes/syncing.md#replacing-a-window)), `pipe.get_rowcount(estimate=True)`, `pipe.verify_schema()`, `mrsm.Pipeline`, and unknown-kwarg warnings in `get_data()`.

**Removed internals** (raise `ImportError` naming the replacement):

| Removed | Replacement |
|---|---|
| `meerschaum.connectors.sql._pipes`, `_users`, `_plugins`, `_fetch`, `_partition`, `_compress`, `_maintenance` | Public `SQLConnector` methods (`_sql`, `_create_engine`, `_uri`, `tables.get_tables`, `_users.valid_username` stay) |
| `SQLConnector.get_add_columns_queries`, `get_alter_columns_queries`, `get_to_sql_dtype`, `create_pipe_table_from_df` | None (Rust generates DDL internally) |
| `meerschaum.actions.<module>` and `meerschaum.api.routes.*` | `meerschaum.actions.actions['<name>']` / `mrsm.entry([...])` |
| `Daemon(target=...)`, `run_daemon`, `daemon_action`, `daemon_entry` | `meerschaum.jobs.Job` (read/control `Daemon` façade stays) |
| `meerschaum.utils.packages.dash` | List `dash` in `required` and call `attempt_import('dash')` |

`meerschaum.utils.sql` and standard plugin SDK helpers (`SuccessTuple`, `attempt_import`, `Venv`, `make_connector`, `make_action`, hooks, `User`, `Token`) are preserved.

## Teams, access, and permissions

- **Roles & registration:** The first API user is admin; self-registration is then disabled unless `api.permissions.registration.users: true`. Default role is `editor` (`api.permissions.default_role`): **Viewer** reads; **Editor** manages pipes/SQL and starts jobs; **Operator** adds actions, web terminal (`webterm:use`), and job management. Legacy `api.permissions.actions.non_admin: true` maps to Operator; `--secure` restricts actions and terminal to admins.
- **Tokens & teams:** Tokens are capped at their owner's current scopes (`scopes=[]` grants nothing; `*` is stored literally). Every user belongs to **Everyone**, connectors accept `teams: [...]`, and `access` and `locks` are now **reserved pipe parameter keys**.
- **Locks & protected connectors:** Pipe locks apply locally and cannot be bypassed by `--force`, `-y`, or `--allow-protected` (`mrsm unlock pipes --locks sync`). Connectors with `protected: true` block all writes unless `--allow-protected`, `MRSM_ALLOW_PROTECTED=1`, or `allow_protected()` is active.

See [Access and locks](pipes/access-and-locks.md), [Permissions](api-instance/permissions.md), [Teams](api-instance/teams.md), and [Tokens](api-instance/tokens.md#scopes).

## Plugin authors

Data plugins (`fetch`, `sync`, `register`, `setup`), `@make_action`, hooks, `@make_connector`, and per-plugin venvs keep their v4 interfaces. Key updates:

- **Worker processes & `-P`:** CLI and server runs execute Python plugins in a long-lived worker launched with `-P` (cwd is not on `sys.path`). Do not assume fresh module globals per command, and keep helper modules inside `MRSM_PLUGINS_DIR` or installed packages.
- **Declare dependencies:** The base `mrsm` venv no longer pre-installs `pandas`, `requests`, `dash`, `plotly`, `rich`, `dask`, etc. Declare everything in `required = [...]`. Audit and clean venvs with `mrsm show venvs` and `mrsm prune venvs --dry`; run `mrsm install required <plugin>` after upgrading Python minor versions.
- **Manifests & actions:** Decorators cache in a plugin manifest (`mrsm reload` rebuilds it). `@make_action(name='weather wait')` supports multi-word actions, and any action repeats under `--loop` automatically unless it defines a `loop` parameter.
- **Streaming & graph windows:** Graph runs may pass chunk-aligned historical `begin`/`end` windows. Custom `IS_INSTANCE = True` connectors can implement `acquire_pipe_lease` / `release_pipe_lease`. Legacy `--listen` keeps working, or switch to `IS_STREAMING = True` with `subscribe(pipe, sink)` for engine-managed micro-batching and post-commit acks:

```python
IS_STREAMING = True

def subscribe(pipe, sink, **kw):
    client.on_message = lambda m: sink.push([parse(m)], token=m.mid)
    client.connect(...)
    client.loop_forever()
```

- **API plugins (`@api_plugin`) & MCP:** Python routes and `meerschaum.mcp.tool` handlers run in a Python API host behind the Rust proxy (needs `meerschaum[api]`). Core routes live in Rust: replace core middleware with `api.permissions.rate_limits` or NGINX, and replace route-stripping hooks with `api.permissions.routes.allowlist`/`disabled` or `--public` ([Permissions](api-instance/permissions.md#the-public-preset)). Plugin routes aren't in `/openapi.json`, and `api.dash.sessions` IDs must be UUID strings. New helpers: `session_user`, `optional_session_user`, `mount_static` ([Web Pages](plugins/web-pages.md)), `meerschaum.utils.cache` ([Caching](plugins/caching.md)), and `meerschaum.testing` ([Testing](plugins/testing.md)).
- **Dash plugins (`@dash_plugin` / `@web_page`):** Requires `meerschaum[dash]` (declare `dash-daq` in `required` if used). `/dash` is now the Overview; the old dashboard is at `/dash/terminal`. Console callbacks require a signed-in session—mark public ones with `@dash_plugin(public=True)` or `@web_callback(..., public=True)` (or set `api.dash.callbacks_require_session: false`).

### Option B: the page contract (recommended for new pages)

Return an HTML fragment from `@web_page` to build console pages that work identically in Python and Rust plugins. The console frames your fragment at `/dash/<path>` and bundles Plotly.js 4 (`meerschaum.plugins.figure(fig)`), MapLibre GL JS (`<div data-mrsm-map='...'>`, requires WebGL2), and [HTMX](https://htmx.org) locally—no CDN needed.

```python
from html import escape
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from meerschaum.plugins import web_page, api_plugin, figure
import plotly.graph_objects as go

def counts_figure(site):
    df = counts_pipe.get_data(params={'site': site} if site != 'all' else None)
    return figure(go.Figure(go.Scatter(x=df['ts'], y=df['count'])))

@web_page('counts', login_required=True, page_group='Reports')
def counts_page():
    opts = ''.join(f'<option value="{escape(v)}">{escape(l)}</option>' for v, l in site_options())
    return f'''
      <select name="site" hx-get="/acme/counts/figure" hx-target="#acme-fig" hx-trigger="change">
        {opts}
      </select>
      <div id="acme-fig">{counts_figure('all')}</div>
    '''

@api_plugin
def init_api(app):
    @app.get('/acme/counts/figure', response_class=HTMLResponse)
    def counts_figure_route(site: str = 'all'):
        return counts_figure(site)
```

- `login_required=True` (default) is enforced before your function runs (`401` otherwise). Page functions take no arguments; read query params or `session_user` in `@api_plugin` routes called by HTMX.
- Use `mrsm-theme-*` CSS classes for light/dark themes, and Plotly.js 4 trace names (`scattermap`/`layout.map` instead of `scattermapbox`/`layout.mapbox`).

**Rust plugins.** Write native plugins as a single `.rs` file or Cargo `cdylib` using `meerschaum-plugin` (replaces a same-named Python plugin and runs on `:slim` images when prebuilt). See [Rust plugins](plugins/rust-plugins.md) and the [advanced guide](plugins/rust-plugins/advanced.md).

## Deployment

- **Docker & stack:** Multi-arch (`amd64`/`arm64`) `bmeares/meerschaum` (`[full]`, with `curl`/`git`/`ssh`) and `:slim` (base wheel + `curl`). `mrsm stack` pins `bmeares/meerschaum:<version>-full`, mounts `create-extensions.sql` as a single file so TimescaleDB init/tuning runs on new volumes, stores secrets in `<root>/stack/secrets/`, and verifies `PG_VERSION` before starting `db`. Update existing DBs with `mrsm upgrade extensions` or `mrsm upgrade postgres` ([Stack](stack/index.md), [Stack upgrades](stack/upgrades.md)).
- **Native HTTPS:** Pass `--keyfile privkey.pem --certfile fullchain.pem` (or `api.server.ssl_*`) to serve HTTPS via rustls with automatic 30 s / `SIGHUP` certificate reload (`308` redirect from plain HTTP, except `/healthcheck`).
- **Web terminal & GUI:** Served by the Rust API on a private tmux server under `MRSM_ROOT_DIR` (`api.webterm.tmux.config` to customize). Reverse proxies must forward `Host` / `X-Forwarded-Host` or WebSockets return `403`. `mrsm start gui` opens `pywebview` against a local `--no-auth` loopback API—avoid on shared machines.
- **Security & Windows:** Plugin archives reject symlink/hardlink members; HTTP MCP SQL blocks internal `mrsm_*` tables and SQL-text functions ([MCP security](mcp/security.md)). Windows runs the API host over loopback TCP (routes and Dash work), while background jobs (`-d`) still require Linux, macOS, Docker, or WSL.
- **Rollback:** Keep v4.1 in a separate venv—both versions share the same root and instance layout (set `meerschaum:executor: local` if moving back from systemd). Run `mrsm deduplicate pipes` to clean up legacy v4 SQLite/NULL-upsert duplicates.


---

# 📖 Glossary

Source: https://meerschaum.io/reference/glossary/

# 📖 Glossary

This page defines the core Meerschaum domain terms in one place. Each entry links to its reference documentation where one exists. Other pages can deep-link to any term by its heading anchor, e.g. [`#upsert`](#upsert).

---

### Action

A top-level command such as `sync`, `show`, or `register`, implemented as a module in `meerschaum/actions/`. Every action returns a [`SuccessTuple`](#successtuple). Plugins add actions with the `@make_action` decorator.

### Subaction

A noun-specific variant of an [action](#action), auto-discovered by naming convention (e.g. `sync pipes` → `sync_pipes`). New subactions need no registration, just define `def <action>_<subaction>(**kwargs) -> SuccessTuple`.

### Backtrack (`backtrack_minutes`)

The overlapping window between syncs (default 1440 minutes), set under `parameters['fetch']['backtrack_minutes']`. During a [sync](#sync), rows are fetched starting from the last sync time *minus* this interval, so slower or backlogged data streams are not missed. See [Backtracking](/reference/pipes/syncing/#backtracking).

### Chunk (`chunk_minutes`)

The interval into which a [verification sync](#verification-sync) divides a pipe's range (default 43200 minutes, 30 days), set under `parameters['verify']['chunk_minutes']`. It is also the authoritative width for [native partitioning](#native-partitioning). Aliases: `chunk_hours`/`chunk_days`/`chunk_weeks`/`chunk_years`/`chunk_seconds`. See [Verification Syncs](/reference/pipes/syncing/#verification-syncs).

### Columns

The `parameters['columns']` dictionary maps a semantic *role* to a column name. The key roles are:

- **`datetime`**, the column driving incremental sync (the begin/end window); defines the [datetime axis](#datetime-axis).
- **`id`**, forms the composite uniqueness key alongside `datetime`.
- **`primary`**, the primary-key column.
- **`value`**, the measured value column.

Pipes without a `datetime` column still work but lose incremental behavior. See [Columns](/reference/pipes/parameters/).

### Connector

The interface Meerschaum uses to fetch and insert data and to read/write metadata. A connector is identified by [connector keys](#connector-keys) (`type:label`, e.g. `sql:main`). See [Connectors](/reference/connectors/).

### Connector keys

The two-part identifier of a [connector](#connector): its **type** and **label** joined by a colon, e.g. `sql:main` (type `sql`, label `main`) or `plugin:noaa`. As a pipe's first key, the connector keys name the data source.

### Datetime axis

The time dimension of a pipe, defined by the [`datetime` column](#columns). It may be a real timestamp (dtype `datetime`, stored as `TIMESTAMPTZ`) or an integer epoch (dtype `int`). Incremental syncs, chunking, and [native partitioning](#native-partitioning) all operate along this axis.

### Dtypes

The `parameters['dtypes']` dictionary mapping column names to Meerschaum dtype strings: `datetime`, `int`, `numeric`, `uuid`, `json`, `bytes`, `geometry[srid]`, or any valid Pandas dtype (e.g. `Int64`, `float64`, `bool`). Incoming data is cast to these during [sync](#sync). See [Parameters](/reference/pipes/parameters/).

### Executor

The backend that runs a [job](#job), set via `executor_keys`: `local` (a managed daemon process), `systemd` (a user service), or `api:label` (posted to a remote API instance). See [Jobs](/reference/background-jobs/).

### Hypercore / Columnstore

A TimescaleDB columnstore feature. With `hypercore=True` (default), the columnstore is enabled at `CREATE TABLE` and a columnstore policy is auto-created; `False` yields a plain row-store [hypertable](#hypertable). The columnstore policy *is* the compression policy (`compress`).

### Hypertable

Set by `parameters['hypertable']` (default `True`). On TimescaleDB, the target table is created as a hypertable. On other flavors supporting range partitioning (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, MySQL/MariaDB, MSSQL), datetime-axis pipes are range-partitioned by default, see [native partitioning](#native-partitioning). Set `False` to opt out. Only newly created tables are affected.

### In-place sync

A [sync](#sync) of a `sql:`-connector pipe whose data never leaves the database: the fetch, filter, and upsert all execute as SQL on the instance, avoiding a round-trip through the Meerschaum process.

### Instance connector

The [connector](#connector) where a pipe's metadata *and* data are stored, a pipe's 4th key (`instance=`/`mrsm_instance=`). Must implement the pipes/users/plugins/tokens interface (`IS_INSTANCE = True`). Implementations: `SQLConnector`, `APIConnector`, `ValkeyConnector`. See [Instances and Repositories](/reference/connectors/#instances-and-repositories).

### Job

A background process wrapping `sysargs`, run via `meerschaum.jobs.Job(name, sysargs, executor_keys=...)`. Jobs persist across restarts and stream logs; `start()`/`stop()`/`pause()` return a [`SuccessTuple`](#successtuple). See [Background Jobs](/reference/background-jobs/) and [executor](#executor).

### Location key

A pipe's optional third key (default `None`), used to tag or shard a data stream (e.g. a station or region). Two pipes sharing a [connector](#connector) and [metric](#metric-key) but differing in location are distinct pipes.

### Metric key

A pipe's second key, a label for the data stream it represents (e.g. `weather`, `sales`).

### `MRSM{}` config symlink

A reference to a configuration value inside pipe parameters or connector URIs, written `MRSM{key1:key2:key3}` and resolved at access time. For example, `MRSM{meerschaum:connectors:sql:main:password}` resolves to the configured password.

### Native partitioning

The default behavior (from `hypertable=True`) of range-partitioning a datetime-axis pipe's target table on its [datetime column](#columns) for flavors that support it (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, MySQL/MariaDB, MSSQL). Partition width reuses [`verify.chunk_minutes`](#chunk-chunk_minutes), with epoch-aligned (deterministic) boundaries. Partitions are auto-created during sync. See [Maintenance](/reference/pipes/maintenance/).

### Parameters

The central `pipe.parameters` metadata dictionary holding `columns`, `dtypes`, `indices`, `tags`, `fetch`, `verify`, `sql`, `target`, and behavioral flags (`upsert`, `hypertable`, `enforce`, etc.). Mutate in memory with `pipe.update_parameters({...}, persist=False)`; persist with `pipe.edit()` or `persist=True`. See [Parameters](/reference/pipes/parameters/).

### Pipe

A named data stream synced into a table, identified by three keys ([connector](#connector-keys), [metric](#metric-key), and [location](#location-key)) plus an [instance connector](#instance-connector) where its metadata and data live. The central abstraction in Meerschaum. See [Pipes](/reference/pipes/).

### Plugin

A Python file or package in `MRSM_PLUGINS_DIR` that extends Meerschaum. Recognized hooks include `register`, `fetch`, `sync`, and `setup`; decorators include `@make_action`, `@api_plugin`, `@dash_plugin`, and `@web_page`. See [Plugins](/reference/plugins/types-of-plugins/).

### Repository connector

A subset of [instance connectors](#instance-connector) used to host and distribute [plugins](#plugin). Repository connectors may only be `api` connectors. See [Instances and Repositories](/reference/connectors/#instances-and-repositories).

### Source connector

The [connector](#connector) named by a pipe's [connector keys](#connector-keys), the origin of the pipe's data (e.g. `sql:main`, `plugin:noaa`). Distinct from the [instance connector](#instance-connector), which stores the result.

### `SuccessTuple`

The universal return type `Tuple[bool, str]` used by actions, pipe methods, and connector methods, e.g. `(True, "Success")` or `(False, "reason")`. Action-level code returns a `SuccessTuple` rather than raising.

### Sync

The main ETL entry point, `pipe.sync(df=None, begin='', end=None, ...)`, in three stages: **fetch** new rows, **filter** out already-seen rows, and **upsert** the remainder into the [instance connector](#instance-connector). See [Syncing](/reference/pipes/syncing/).

### Tags

A list of labels (`parameters['tags']`) for grouping pipes, usable as a selection filter (e.g. `show pipes --tags foo`). Prefix a tag with `_` to negate it. See [Tags](/reference/pipes/tags/).

### Target (table)

The table name a pipe writes to (`pipe.target`). Default: `{connector_keys with ':' → '_'}_{metric_key}` (plus `_{location_key}` when set). Override via `parameters['target']`. On SQL instances the full name is `schema.target`.

### Upsert

When `parameters['upsert']` is `True`, inserts and updates are combined into a single query and a unique index is created on the [columns](#columns). On partitioned tables the conflict target must include the [datetime column](#datetime-axis). See [`upsert`](/reference/pipes/parameters/#upsert).

### Verification sync

A more thorough [sync](#sync) (`verify pipes` / `pipe.verify()`) that divides a pipe's entire interval into [chunks](#chunk-chunk_minutes) and re-syncs each, comparing remote vs. local row counts to re-sync only mismatched chunks. See [Verification Syncs](/reference/pipes/syncing/#verification-syncs).

### `{{ Pipe() }}` syntax

A templating syntax for referencing another pipe from within pipe parameters (notably the `sql` definition), e.g. `{{ Pipe('plugin:noaa', 'weather') }}`, which resolves to the referenced pipe's [target table](#target-table) at query time. Supports attribute chains (`{{ Pipe('a', 'b').columns['datetime'] }}`) and self-reference (`{{ self.parameters['key'] }}`).


---

# Python

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/

# Python

Install the package, then import the SDK:

```bash
python -m pip install meerschaum
```

```python
import meerschaum as mrsm
```

The package includes the native engine and `mrsm` command. Plain dictionaries work without a DataFrame library. Install `meerschaum[polars]` or `meerschaum[pandas]` when you want those frames.

| Next | What you build |
|---|---|
| [Pipes](pipes.md) | Sync and read local rows |
| [Pipelines](pipelines.md) | Save, plan, and run a workflow |
| [Plugins](plugins.md) | Fetch from a custom source |

[Browse the complete Python API](https://docs.meerschaum.io), including signatures and module documentation.


---

# Pipes

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/pipes/

# Pipes in Python

A Pipe stores a named data stream on an instance. This example uses the built-in local SQLite instance and supplies its own rows:

```python
import meerschaum as mrsm

pipe = mrsm.Pipe(
    'plugin:manual', 'readings', instance='sql:local',
    columns={'id': 'id'},
)
result = pipe.sync([{'id': 1, 'temperature': 21.5}])
if not result.success:
    raise RuntimeError(result.message)

print(result.inserted, result.updated)
print(pipe.get_data(as_docs=True))
```

Sync the same row again to update it without adding a duplicate. Supply `columns={'datetime': 'ts', 'id': 'id'}` for a timestamped stream.

## Read a window

`begin` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive:

```python
rows = pipe.get_data(as_docs=True, params={'id': [1, 2]}, limit=10)
print(pipe.get_rowcount())
```

For a Pipe with a datetime column:

```python
rows = pipe.get_data(as_docs=True, begin='2026-01-01', end='2026-02-01')
```

## Find existing Pipes

```python
pipes = mrsm.get_pipes(instance='sql:local', tags=['daily'], as_list=True)
for pipe in pipes:
    print(pipe)
```

See [Pipe parameters](../../reference/pipes/parameters.md), [reading data](../../reference/pipes/reading.md), and the full [Pipe API](https://docs.meerschaum.io/meerschaum.html#Pipe).


---

# Pipelines

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/pipelines/

# Pipelines in Python

A Pipeline selects Pipes and runs their dependencies in order. Once your Pipes are registered, save a workflow on their instance:

```python
import meerschaum as mrsm

pipe = mrsm.Pipe('sql:local', 'fahrenheit', instance='sql:local')
pipeline = mrsm.Pipeline(pipe, parents=True, instance='sql:local')
print(pipeline.plan())

success, message = pipeline.save('climate')
if not success:
    raise RuntimeError(message)
run = pipeline.sync()
print(run.run_id, run.success, run.inserted, run.updated)
```

The [first Pipeline tutorial](../../get-started/pipelines.md) creates the source and transformation used here.

## Load and schedule

```python
pipeline = mrsm.Pipeline('climate', instance='sql:local')
print(pipeline.get_runs())
job = pipeline.schedule('every 10 minutes')
```

A saved definition keeps member references and execution settings. A Job supplies a schedule. Deleting a Pipeline definition keeps its member Pipes and their data.

See [Pipeline operations](../../reference/pipelines/index.md) and the full [Python API](https://docs.meerschaum.io).


---

# Plugins

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/python/plugins/

# Python plugins

Save `readings.py` in your plugins directory, or use `mrsm bootstrap plugins readings` to create it:

```python
__version__ = '0.1.0'

def register(pipe, **kwargs):
    return {'columns': {'id': 'id'}}

def fetch(pipe, begin=None, end=None, **kwargs):
    return [{'id': 1, 'temperature': 21.5}]
```

Register and sync a Pipe:

```bash
mrsm register pipe -c plugin:readings -m readings -i sql:local
mrsm sync pipes -c plugin:readings -i sql:local
```

`register` supplies initial parameters; `fetch` supplies rows. Keep optional arguments in `**kwargs`, and use `begin` / `end` to limit work for larger sources.

??? info "Dependencies and deployment"
    Declare packages in `required = ['requests']`, install them with `mrsm install required readings`, and keep heavy imports inside functions. For repeatable deployments, pin dependency versions and use the [environment controls](../../reference/environment.md#mrsm_no_auto_install).

Continue with [plugin functions](../../reference/plugins/writing-plugins.md), [web pages](../../reference/plugins/web-pages.md), or [plugin repositories](../../reference/plugins/repositories.md). Full module documentation is at [docs.meerschaum.io](https://docs.meerschaum.io/meerschaum/plugins.html).


---

|---|---|

| Select dependencies and run the engine | [Pipelines](pipelines.md) |
| Add a command or data source | [Plugins](plugins.md) |

Use the public `meerschaum` crate for applications. Use `meerschaum-plugin` for packaged native plugins. The other implementation crates may change between minor releases.

[Complete Rust API reference](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/) · [Plugin SDK](https://docs.rs/meerschaum-plugin/latest/meerschaum_plugin/)

# Embedding

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/embedding/

# Embed Meerschaum

Library applications disable default features to avoid building the full CLI:

```toml
[dependencies]
meerschaum = { version = "5", default-features = false, features = ["sql", "engine"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
```

| Feature | Adds |
|---|---|
| `sql` | Native SQL connectors |
| `engine` | Pipelines, plans, runs, and execution history |
| `api` | Client for a Meerschaum HTTP instance |
| `valkey` | Valkey connector |
| `plugin` | Native plugin SDK |
| `server` | HTTP server |

The default `cli` feature builds the standalone `mrsm` command. Keep it off for a library unless you need that command-line surface.

## Construct a Pipe

```rust
use meerschaum::Pipe;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let pipe = Pipe::builder("plugin:manual", "readings")
        .instance("sql:demo")
        .build()?;
    println!("{pipe}");
    Ok(())
}
```

Continue with [syncing rows](pipes.md). For engine configuration and run options, browse [the engine module](https://docs.rs/meerschaum-engine/latest/meerschaum_engine/).


---

# Pipes

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/pipes/

# Pipes in Rust

This local example provides rows directly and writes them through the SQL connector. Use the dependencies from [Embedding](embedding.md).

```rust
use meerschaum::{Frame, InstanceConnector, Pipe, SqlConnector, SyncOptions};
use meerschaum::kernel::value::Value as Cell;
use meerschaum::sql::uri::ConnectionSpec;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let spec = ConnectionSpec::from_uri("sqlite:///demo.db", Some("demo"), None)?;
    let conn = SqlConnector::connect("demo", spec).await?;
    let pipe = Pipe::builder("plugin:manual", "readings")
        .instance("sql:demo")
        .build()?;
    let rows = Frame::from_object_columns(vec![
        ("id".into(), vec![Cell::Int(1)]),
        ("temperature".into(), vec![Cell::Float(21.5)]),
    ])?;
    let result = InstanceConnector::sync_pipe(
        &conn, &pipe, rows, &SyncOptions::default(),
    ).await;
    println!("{result:?}");
    Ok(())
}
```

`Frame` accepts Arrow record batches too. `InstanceConnector` exposes the same operations across SQL, API, and Valkey instances; select the matching Cargo feature.

See [Frame](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/struct.Frame.html), [InstanceConnector](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/trait.InstanceConnector.html), and [SqlConnector](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/struct.SqlConnector.html) for method signatures.


---

# Pipelines

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/pipelines/

# Pipelines in Rust

The engine takes a connector registry, a home instance, and run options. Its selection chooses targets and how far to traverse their dependencies.

This helper runs registered Pipes on an existing SQL connection:

```rust
use std::sync::Arc;
use meerschaum::{Engine, RunOptions, SqlConnector};
use meerschaum::engine::{Depth, EngineConfig, PipeRef, Selection, StaticRegistry};

async fn run_reporting(conn: Arc<SqlConnector>) {
    let registry = Arc::new(
        StaticRegistry::new()
            .with_instance("sql:demo", conn.clone())
            .with_source("sql:demo", conn),
    );
    let engine = Engine::new(registry, EngineConfig {
        home_instance: "sql:demo".into(),
        ..Default::default()
    });
    let target = PipeRef::new("sql:demo", "sql:demo", "reporting", None);
    let options = RunOptions {
        selection: Some(Selection::refs([target]).with_parents(Some(Depth::All))),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    println!("{:?}", engine.plan(&options).await);
    let result = engine.run(options).await;
    println!("{:?}", result);
}
```

Register the sources and transformations before calling the helper. If definitions use `{{ Pipe(...) }}` SQL templates, supply the registry's `with_table_reference` resolver for the connector's identifier rules.

## Plan, run, inspect

`Engine::plan` reads the graph and current state. `Engine::run` executes independent branches concurrently and persists run history by default. `RunOptions` controls bounds, workers, rebuild approval, and selection.

The root-level reexports are the stable Rust interface. The implementation module used for registry and selection helpers may change in a minor release, so pin the crate version when depending on those details.

See [Engine](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/struct.Engine.html), [RunOptions](https://docs.rs/meerschaum/latest/meerschaum/struct.RunOptions.html), and [engine internals](https://docs.rs/meerschaum-engine/latest/meerschaum_engine/) for full signatures. The [operational Pipeline guide](../../reference/pipelines/index.md) explains planning, backfills, and recovery.


---

# Plugins

Source: https://meerschaum.io/docs/rust/plugins/

# Rust plugins

A single-file plugin needs no Cargo project. Save `greetings.rs` in your plugins directory:

```rust
/// Say hello.
#[make_action]
fn greet() {
    println!("Hello from Rust!");
}
```

Run `mrsm greet`. Meerschaum builds the plugin when needed; a Rust toolchain is required for the first build and after edits.

## Supply rows

Save `readings.rs`:

```rust
fn register() -> Value {
    json!({"columns": {"id": "id"}})
}

fn fetch() -> Vec<Value> {
    vec![json!({"id": 1, "temperature": 21.5})]
}
```

```bash
mrsm register pipe -c plugin:readings -m readings -i sql:local
mrsm sync pipes -c plugin:readings -i sql:local
```

Single-file plugins receive `Value`, `json!`, and the marker macros from their host. For connectors, hooks, packaged plugins, or host calls, continue to the [Rust plugin guide](../../reference/plugins/rust-plugins.md) and [SDK reference](https://docs.rs/meerschaum-plugin/latest/meerschaum_plugin/).

# v5

Source: https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v5/

# Meerschaum 5

## 5.1.6

- **Reduce WAL from PostgreSQL syncs.**  
  Frame updates and upserts of up to 1,024 rows use bound arrays. Larger patches use a transaction-local staging table that PostgreSQL removes after the merge. SQL-to-SQL syncs use unlogged staging on PostgreSQL, PostGIS, and TimescaleDB.

- **Expire engine history once per SQL instance.**  
  TimescaleDB drops whole chunks during automatic expiry and keeps the chunk containing the cutoff. Sync metrics inherit `system.engine.run_history_days`. Set `metrics_retention_days` under `system.engine` to keep a different window, or set it to `30` to retain the previous policy. See [Sync metrics](../reference/api-instance/sync-metrics.md).

- **Choose which loop laps to store.**  
  Set `system.engine.persist_skipped_laps: false` to omit successful all-skipped laps from run history. Live events and job heartbeats still report those laps.

- **Share Python workers and job hosts.**  
  Callback-based stream pipes on one connector can opt into `stream.shared_worker`. Use `: --loop --independent-laps` to run several actions in one job with separate intervals and retries. Linux worker recycling now includes swapped private pages in its memory limit. See [Continuous mode](../reference/pipelines/continuous.md) and [Background jobs](../reference/background-jobs/index.md).

- **Finish native plugin migrations cleanly.**  
  A native plugin owns its name, including sync hooks. Meerschaum warns once when it shadows a Python plugin and reports a fallback if the native plugin fails to load. See [Rust plugins](/reference/plugins/rust-plugins/).

- **Bound sync hooks and their telemetry.**  
  Hook writes keep their latest sync status and skip the metrics queue. Set `system.engine.sync_hook_timeout_seconds` to adjust the five-second limit for each hook phase.

- **Apply retention and compression edits.**  
  A bare `--end '16 days ago'` now advances every midnight. `clear pipes` prints the resolved bounds. TimescaleDB syncs apply declared chunk widths to future chunks and reconcile the columnstore policy with `compress.after`.

- **Report incomplete job deletions.**  
  `delete jobs` removes named, retired job directories, reports missing names, and cleans up the installed link for a scoped systemd unit.

## 5.1.5

### Before upgrading

- **Preview five-field cron schedules.**  
  Use 5.1.5 to check upcoming runs before rolling it out. A job can now run on a date that earlier versions skipped. Both plain and zoned schedules are affected. A quarterly 03:00 UTC job started on November 24 after 03:00 now runs on January 1, then April 1. Earlier versions skipped January.

  ```bash
  mrsm show schedule '0 3 1 1,4,7,10 *' 4
  ```

### Fixes

- **Keep elevation on PostGIS updates.**  
  PostGIS table inspection preserves Z, M, and ZM dimensions on `geometry` and `geography` columns. Ordinary SQL-to-SQL sync updates an existing aggregated 3D target when only elevation changes under normal dtype enforcement.

- **Keep console team choices across reloads.**  
  Administrators default to **All teams (Admin)** on initial login. Selecting **Everyone** previews that team's view, and an explicit choice persists after reload. An empty instance selector explains the available choices.

- **Use the exact connector in SDK lookups.**  
  The SDK refreshes a user and a token's owner from the exact connector instance supplied, even when another database shares the same connector label.

- **Fix Windows hangs and preserve drive letters in plugin paths.**  
  Windows users can run `mrsm show actions` with Python plugins installed, access plugin routes and the Dash console after starting the API, and use drive-letter paths in [`MRSM_PLUGINS_DIR`](../reference/environment.md#mrsm_plugins_dir).

- **Handle daylight saving time in cron schedules.**  
  The Python scheduler honors recognized local abbreviations such as `EST` and `EDT` across daylight saving time on systems that support abbreviations. Starting a wildcard-hour cron during a repeated hour keeps the remaining runs in both occurrences of the hour. A specific time in a skipped hour runs right when the clock jumps past the gap. See [Schedules](../reference/background-jobs/schedules.md).

- **Return errors in the Rust transaction example.**  
  The native Rust plugin transaction example shows how to return an error on an unsuccessful statement so earlier writes roll back. See [Advanced Rust Plugins](../reference/plugins/rust-plugins/advanced.md).

- **Expand release checks.**  
  Release checks now cover an isolated team member registering, using, and revoking a scoped token with a live Valkey cache. They also verify existing 3D rows and persisted data across version upgrades.

## 5.1.4

- **Register and manage tokens from isolated teams.**  
  Isolated team members can [list and manage their tokens](../reference/api-instance/tokens.md#web-ui) in the Web Console. **Register** saves the token to the API server's store and shows its credentials in the result dialog.

## 5.1.3

Patch release making untagged (**Everyone**) pipes and saved Pipelines on team-reserved instances usable by the reserved teams with no backfill.

- **Use untagged pipes on reserved instances.**  
  On any instance connector with `teams: [...]`, **Everyone** now covers members of the reserved teams—including isolated teams, terminals, jobs, and MCP clients. Pipes and saved Pipelines from `mrsm compose`, plugins, CLI, or ported databases work immediately without rewriting stored `access` ([Reserve an instance for teams](../reference/api-instance/teams.md#reserve-an-instance-for-teams)).

  ```yaml
  connectors:
    sql:
      observations:
        flavor: sqlite
        database: observations.db
        teams: [wetlands, water_quality]
  ```

- **Roles, locks, and live updates apply automatically.**  
  Reserved-team managers can edit access, lock/unlock, and view private untagged pipes, while per-pipe owners, `private` visibility, `owner`-only edits, and locks hold as before. Visibility `everyone` covers every reserved team, and reservation edits, renames, or deletions take effect on the next request ([Access and Locks](../reference/pipes/access-and-locks.md#access)).

- **Clearer console views.**  
  The **Access** dialog lists which teams **Everyone** covers on a reserved instance, **My teams** includes those untagged pipes, and the **Team** switcher matches what isolated members see.

## 5.1.2

Maintenance release: leaner Docker images that share layers, stricter non-admin SQL checks, faster API reads on large SQL instances, and console, web terminal, and sync fixes.

### Before upgrading from 5.1.1

- **Non-admin SQL checks are stricter.** Non-admin queries and pipe definitions over the API or MCP are now refused if *any* SQL dialect would parse them as multi-statement or mutating (such as `;` inside `$$...$$`, or a write keyword after `#` or space-less `--`). Admins and local `mrsm` commands are unaffected.
- **Docker images always run as `1000:1000`.** Release images no longer inherit the build host's UID/GID.
- **Standalone SQL `port` values must be integers.** Values like `abc`, `true`, or `5432.0` are refused instead of silently falling back to a default port. If you set a `uri`, Meerschaum uses the URI's port.

### Highlights & Fixes

- **Leaner Docker images with shared layers.**  
  `full`, `rust-full`, `slim`, and `rust` now share common layers (`mrsm`, the Python wheel, and the Rust compiler snapshot) and keep OS layers stable across patch releases, so `docker pull` downloads only what changed.

  ```bash
  docker pull bmeares/meerschaum:5.1.2-full
  ```

- **Smaller `mrsm` binary.**  
  Release binaries and wheels drop unused Arrow/Polars features and strip symbol tables (~111 MB vs. ~135 MB). Panic backtraces still show the error message and source location.

- **Faster API reads on large SQL instances.**  
  Pipe data and CSV requests now look up a single pipe by key instead of scanning the full catalog on SQL and Valkey instances.

- **Hardened SQL comment checks.**  
  API and MCP SQL validation checks every dialect's comment syntax so internal tables hidden behind `#`, `--`, or nested `/* */` comments are blocked everywhere.

- **Console & web terminal fixes.**  
  - Console calls to the API ignore `HTTP_PROXY` and redirects so session credentials stay local.
  - Job log streams renew their session authorization while open and stop immediately if credentials are rotated or revoked.
  - The **Users & Teams** page follows the selected team in the team switcher (choose **All teams (Admin)** to manage everyone).
  - Isolated team permissions are computed in one place across all console pages.
  - Web terminal fixes: a refused window no longer blocks future windows, API-only panes set `TERM`, and closed sessions stop reconnecting.

- **Sync, job, and database fixes.**  
  - **Remote action results:** Log streams wait up to 2 seconds for a finished job's supervisor to save its result (and clients fall back to reading the saved result), eliminating spurious `No result available.` replies on busy hosts.
  - **Startup pauses:** Pausing a job while it is still starting keeps its supervisor active so it can still stop cleanly when the executor exits.
  - **SQLite / GeoPackage schema reload:** Pooled connections reload table schemas after a sync adds columns, preventing newly added columns from reading back with literal quotes.
  - **In-place syncs:** A pipe whose source is the engine's home database but whose instance is elsewhere no longer runs in-place on the source database.
  - **Engine metrics & Oracle:** Dropped sync metrics now log a rate-limited warning instead of vanishing silently, and Oracle instances keep internal table readiness across index DDL.

- **Switched to released `sqlx 0.9.1` & contributor cleanups.**  
  Dropped the temporary `sqlx` git patch in `Cargo.toml`, consolidated Rust integration tests from 411 binaries down to 45 suites, split oversize Rust modules, and added `scripts/check_architecture.py`, `GLOSSARY.md`, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, and `docs/adr/`.

## 5.1.1

Maintenance release with console UX improvements, credential handling fixes in `stack.yaml`, and Docker stack / isolated-team fixes.

### Before upgrading from 5.1.0

- **Docker stacks:** run `mrsm stack up -d` after upgrading so `api` mounts the public executor directory at `/run/meerschaum/executors/desired` instead of `/meerschaum/executors/desired`. Any root-owned `/meerschaum/executors` placeholder left by 5.1.0 is automatically moved aside to `.executors.root-owned-<n>`.
- **Clean up expanded `stack.yaml` secrets:** if an earlier `mrsm edit config stack` or `write_config()` expanded credentials into `stack.yaml`, replace them with `MRSM{...}` references (e.g. `MRSM{!meerschaum:connectors:sql:main}` or `<DOLLAR>POSTGRES_PASSWORD`).

### Highlights & Fixes

- **Team switcher in the web console.**  
  Administrators and multi-team members now have a **Team** dropdown next to **Instance** to view the console as a specific team (or `Everyone`). Instances, pipes, connectors, plugins, and jobs narrow to that team's view without ever escalating permissions; Actions and the web terminal pause until returning to **All teams**.

- **Nested Pages menu.**  
  Plugin page groups with multiple pages now collapse into sections with page counts (groups with >3 pages start collapsed unless active), drop repeated prefixes, nest sub-paths, and filter by the viewer's allowed plugins.

- **Balanced Overview without Pipelines.**  
  The Overview page keeps Pipes and Connectors balanced across the layout when no Pipelines or syncs exist yet.

- **Preserve `MRSM{...}` references in `stack.yaml`.**  
  Generating `stack.yaml` no longer expands references inside lists (`ports`, healthchecks, Grafana data sources), and `write_config({'stack': get_config('stack')})` preserves `MRSM{!meerschaum}`, `MRSM{!system}`, and `MRSM{!api}` instead of writing plaintext secrets.

- **Externalize secrets for custom API services.**  
  Any Compose service with `MRSM_CONFIG` or `MRSM_PATCH` (such as `api-sra` alongside `api`) now writes secrets to `stack/secrets/<service>/` via `MRSM_CONFIG_FILE` / `MRSM_PATCH_FILE` on 5.1+ images, and cleans up files when a service is removed.

- **Fix `/jobs` HTTP 503 on upgraded 5.1.0 Docker stacks.**  
  Moved the host executor mount from `/meerschaum/executors/desired` to `/run/meerschaum/executors/desired` (`MRSM_EXECUTOR_DESIRED_DIR`), pre-created `/meerschaum/executors` as UID 1000 in all images, and auto-repaired empty root-owned placeholders on startup.

- **Protect team-reserved connectors from host `MRSM_CONFIG`.**  
  Connectors reserved for a team (`teams: [...]`) in an API instance's config are no longer overwritten by same-named host connectors passed through `MRSM_CONFIG` (`MRSM_PATCH` still overrides). **New team** also verifies config writability before creating a database.

- **Fix isolated-team instance fallback and policy warnings.**  
  When `api:permissions:instances` blocks an isolated team's default instance, console pages keep that instance and show one clear alert naming `allow_multiple_instances` / `allowed_instance_keys` instead of falling back to `sql:main`. Creating or editing a team with a blocked instance warns immediately.

- **Propagate Compose `profiles` to `grafana_readonly`.**  
  `grafana_readonly` inherits `profiles` from `db` and `grafana` (with `required: false` on `grafana`'s dependency when profiles differ), and `mrsm doctor` treats a completed exit-0 `grafana_readonly` container as healthy.

## 5.1.0

Security release introducing isolated team execution, read-only Grafana and file-based stack secrets, native Rust plugin SQL/transaction helpers, and immutable sync strategies. See [Teams on One Instance](../reference/api-instance/teams.md) and [Team Execution Environments](../reference/team-executors.md).

### Before upgrading from 5.0.x

- Upgrade the CLI, API host, and Python `meerschaum` package in Team worker interpreters together (5.1.0+ required). On a 5.0.x `--user` install, upgrade with `python3 -m pip install --user --upgrade meerschaum`.
- Review `stack:grafana:readonly_schemas` if dashboards read schemas outside `sql:main`'s owner, then run `mrsm stack up -d` to apply the read-only Grafana role, Valkey password, and secret files.
- Isolated Team commands/terminals require Linux 6.12+ (Landlock ABI 6) and TCP connectors (Unix sockets are denied).

### Highlights

- **Isolated teams, per-team databases, and Grafana orgs.**  
  Create isolated teams with their own PostgreSQL database/schema, roles, connectors, plugin allowlists, and auto-provisioned Grafana orgs via the console or `mrsm bootstrap teams`.

  ```bash
  mrsm bootstrap teams
  ```

- **Sandboxed team execution & optional remote executors (Linux).**  
  Isolated team plugins, jobs, and terminals run with team-only configs, allowlisted environments, per-team venvs, and Landlock + seccomp isolation (`system.engine.python_team_sandbox: auto | require | require_sockets | off`) with optional CPU/memory/disk/egress caps. Administrators can also assign a team to a generated Stack executor or standalone native executor. See [Teams](../reference/api-instance/teams.md) and [Team Execution Environments](../reference/team-executors.md).

- **Restricted non-admin actions & web terminals.**  
  Non-administrators can only execute allowed Meerschaum actions through `/execute`, `/jobs`, MCP, and the web terminal (no arbitrary host shell escapes). See [Permissions](../reference/api-instance/permissions.md).

- **Secrets in files & hardened stack defaults.**  
  Reference secrets dynamically with `MRSM{file:<path>}` and `MRSM{env:<NAME>}`, and pass patches via `MRSM_CONFIG_FILE` / `MRSM_PATCH_FILE`. `mrsm stack` moves API, Grafana, and Valkey credentials out of `docker-compose.yaml` into owner-only files under `<root>/stack/secrets/`, sets a Valkey `requirepass`, and switches Grafana's **Meerschaum Main** data source to a read-only `mrsm__main_ro` role. See [Stack](../reference/stack/index.md) and [Environment](../reference/environment.md).

  ```yaml
  connectors:
    sql:
      main:
        password: MRSM{file:/run/secrets/pg_password}
  ```

- **Immutable sync strategies.**  
  Mark append-only/immutable pipes with `sync.immutable: true` and choose a strategy (`join`, `unbounded-simple`, or monthly corrective). See [Syncing](../reference/pipes/syncing.md#immutable-synchronization-strategies).

- **Native Rust plugin SDK additions (ABI v1 compatible).**  
  Added parameterized SQL (`host::read_sql_with` / `exec_sql_with` with `:name` and native Postgres array binds), host-managed SQL transactions (`host::transaction`), `host::root_dir()`, `Pipe::id()` / `Pipe::is_registered()`, and `#[method]` custom connector methods callable from Python.

- **Time zones in schedules.**  
  Schedules now accept `tz <zone>` (`local`, `utc`, or IANA name) and restore 4.x timezone abbreviations (`EST`/`EDT`, `UTC`) with clean DST handling:

  ```bash
  mrsm sync pipes --schedule "daily starting 21:00 tz America/New_York jitter 5 minutes"
  ```

- **Engine hypertables use 7-day chunks and compression.**  
  Internal engine tables (`mrsm_engine_*`) now default to 7-day chunks, 7-day TimescaleDB compression, and `drop_chunks` retention so expired history reclaims disk space immediately.

- **Faster shell startup & incremental plugin manifests.**  
  Interactive shells and web terminals open immediately from cached manifests and refresh in the background, with per-`MRSM_PLUGINS_DIR` cache keys.

- **Connect an agent from the Tokens page.**  
  The Tokens page generates copy-pasteable MCP configuration for Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, OpenCode, and other clients with the new token's API key filled in.

### Fixes & Improvements

- **PostgreSQL / SQL sync fixes.**  
  Added [`upsert_changed_only`](../reference/pipes/parameters.md#upsert_changed_only) to skip rewriting unchanged rows; fixed PostgreSQL array/enum/extension upserts, in-place syncs without PostGIS, NULL-safe comparisons for non-numeric types, and in-place partitioned/hypertable upserts.
- **Python list SQL parameter binds.**  
  Lists passed to `conn.read(query, params={'ids': [1, 2, 3]})` bind as native PostgreSQL arrays (`= ANY(:ids)`) again rather than `jsonb` (pass `json.dumps(...)` for JSON columns).
- **Safer, clearer `upgrade meerschaum`.**  
  Prompts upfront before downloading, respects `--user` / venv / PEP 668 install locations instead of overwriting system site-packages, and warns about shadowed installs.
- **Jobs, prompts, and connection diagnostics.**  
  Restored interactive `attach job` prompts, in-process `retry_connect()` without leaking passwords in process args, clearer `test_connection(warn=True)` errors, and empty `jobs: {}` in Compose.
- **Helper subprocess sanitization.**  
  Editors, SQL clients, `pip`/`uv`, `cargo`, and `systemctl` no longer inherit `MRSM_CONFIG`, `MRSM_PATCH`, or `MRSM_<TYPE>_<LABEL>` secrets.

## 5.0.x Releases

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Read 5.0.0 – 5.0.2 release notes</summary>

### 5.0.2

- **Performance page selection stability.** Late refresh responses no longer reset the selected window or page.
- **DuckDB download retries.** First-time DuckDB downloads retry twice on transient HTTP/network failures.
- **Public Dash callback warnings.** Startup warns when a `@web_page(login_required=False)` plugin registers callbacks without `public=True`.
- **Dependency updates.** Updated Arrow to 60.1 (`RUSTSEC-2026-0442`) and refreshed Rust dependencies.

### 5.0.1

- **Restart `--restart` jobs on API startup.** Stopped `--restart` jobs resume automatically when the API starts (manually stopped jobs stay stopped).
- **v4 job command compatibility.** Safely reads commands stored in v4 `pickle.pkl` metadata as data without executing pickle code.
- **Security updates.** Updated `rustls-webpki`, `webpki-roots`, `zstd`, `ctutils`, and raised `PyJWT>=2.15.0` for API/Dash extras.

### 5.0.0

Meerschaum 5 rewrites the core engine, SQL/API/Valkey connectors, CLI, HTTP API, job supervisor, and Compose in Rust while keeping your Pipe definitions, configuration, Python plugins, and existing data compatible. See the [migration guide](../reference/migrating-to-v5.md).

- **Dependency-aware Pipelines.**  
  Register, preview, and run parent-before-child DAGs with run history, retries, late-data backfills, and Compose `pipelines:` support. See [Pipelines](../reference/pipelines/index.md).

  ```bash
  mrsm register pipelines daily -i sql:local -c sql:local -m daily --parents
  mrsm plan pipelines daily -i sql:local
  mrsm sync pipelines daily -i sql:local
  mrsm show runs -i sql:local
  ```

- **Expanded Web Console & Grafana dashboards.**  
  Added Overview, Pipelines canvas/runbook, Runs Gantt timeline, Engine performance charts, in-browser plugin editor, token/team/lock management, tmux-tabbed web terminal, and rebuilt **Syncs** + **Engine** Grafana dashboards. See [Web Console](../reference/api-instance/web-console.md).

- **Familiar Python API with Polars default.**  
  `Pipe.sync()` still unpacks to `(success, message)` while exposing `.inserted`, `.updated`, and `.duration` on `SyncResult`. Base installs have zero heavy dependencies (`get_data(as_docs=True)`); new roots default to Polars while existing roots keep pandas.

  ```python
  import meerschaum as mrsm

  pipe = mrsm.Pipe('plugin:manual', 'readings', instance='sql:local', columns={'id': 'id'})
  result = pipe.sync([{'id': 1, 'temperature': 21.5}])
  print(result.success, result.inserted, result.duration)
  print(pipe.get_data(as_docs=True))
  ```

- **Teams, roles, tokens, and Pipe locks.**  
  Added Viewer/Editor/Operator roles, team-scoped access, revocable scoped tokens, and cross-process Pipe locks. Self-registration now closes after creating the first administrator.

- **Rust plugins and embeddable crates.**  
  Write single-file `.rs` or Cargo plugins with the native SDK (`meerschaum-plugin`), or embed `meerschaum-engine` directly in Rust apps. See [Rust Plugins](../reference/plugins/rust-plugins.md).

- **Faster, lower-memory syncs and guided Stack upgrades.**  
  Streamed SQL fetch chunks cut peak RAM nearly in half, column-type caching and native execution speed up small SQL syncs, API shutdown drains cleanly with `/healthcheck/ready`, and `mrsm upgrade/backup/restore postgres` guide Stack maintenance.

</details>

# v4

Source: https://meerschaum.io/changelog/v4/

# Meerschaum 4

Historical release notes for the 4.x series.

## 4.1.0 Releases

<details markdown="1">
<summary>Read release notes</summary>


### v4.1.7

- **Fix starting the API with FastAPI 0.145 or newer.**
  The API passed its tag descriptions to `FastAPI()` under the misspelled keyword `open_api_tags`. Older FastAPI versions silently ignored unknown keywords, but FastAPI 0.145 removed that catch-all, so `start api` failed with "FastAPI.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'open_api_tags'". The keyword is now `openapi_tags`, which also restores the tag descriptions on the API documentation pages.

### v4.1.6

- **Let tokens with `jobs:stop` stop jobs over the API.**
  The stop route required the misspelled scope `josb:stop`, which is not a scope, so only `*` tokens and administrators could stop a job through the API. `POST /jobs/{name}/stop` now requires `jobs:execute` and `jobs:stop`, and a token which explicitly holds the old `josb:stop` is still accepted in place of `jobs:stop`. A refused request names `jobs:stop`.

- **Store `*` literally so it grants every scope.**
  `edit tokens` and `edit users` replaced a typed `*` with the built-in scope list, so an "all scopes" token or user lacked custom (plugin) scopes and any scope added later. `*` is now stored as `*`, which every scope check already honored. The prompts say "`*` grants all scopes, including custom and future scopes", and the "Grant all scopes" switch in the web console's token form registers `*`. `register tokens --scopes '*'` and the token registration route already kept a literal `*`. A token or user created without scopes still gets the built-in list.

- **Let `*` execute actions and jobs for non-admins.**
  The check for permission to run actions and jobs looked for `actions:execute` and `jobs:execute` in the granted scopes, so a non-admin whose scopes were `*` was refused with "Missing scope 'actions:execute'". A literal `*` now satisfies it.

- **Keep `*` when editing a token in the web console.**
  The edit form listed only the built-in scopes, so a token holding `*` showed an empty checklist and saving it replaced `*` with nothing. The form now has the same "Grant all scopes" switch as the registration form, turned on (with the checklist hidden) for a token which holds `*`, and saving keeps `*` unless the switch is turned off.

- **Fix `register tokens --nopretty`.**
  Printing the new token as JSON failed with "Object of type UUID is not JSON serializable". The token's ID and timestamps are now serialized, so the command prints the token and its secret as JSON.

- **Match detached jobs only within their own root directory.**
  When a job's PID file is lost, its process is found by the job's name in the command line. A job with the same name under another `MRSM_ROOT_DIR` matched too, so stopping or killing a job without a PID file could end another root's job. Processes are now matched only if their `MRSM_ROOT_DIR` is this root (unset means the default root). If a process's environment cannot be read, or its root is a relative path, it is still matched as before.

### v4.1.5

- **Stop scanning the process table for completed jobs.**
  When a job has no `process.pid` file, reading its PID searched every running process's command line for the job's name, in case a detached job had lost its PID file. Completed jobs never have a PID file, and a single supervisor pass read the PID of every job many times (while building jobs, checking status and restarts, and formatting), so a production API with retained completed jobs spent most of a CPU core walking the process table every second. A job which recorded that its last run ended is now known to be stopped without any search, constructing a job and formatting it never search the process table, and a search that is needed (a job which began but never recorded an end) is shared by all jobs for two seconds and not repeated for a job which was not found for a minute. Starting, stopping, pausing, resuming, or deleting a job (or recording a new launch from another process) discards the remembered results. A running job which lost its PID file is still found, reported as running, and stoppable: its PID file is written again so later reads are cheap, and processes which started after the job recorded that it began (a reused PID) are ignored. With 20 completed jobs, five supervisor passes with status reads dropped from 3000 process-table scans (108 seconds) to none (under 1 second).

### v4.1.4

- **Don't restart running jobs with a bare `compose start jobs`.**
  v4.1.3 scoped Compose job actions by expanding a bare `compose start jobs` into the project's job names, but naming a running job asks to restart it, so `compose start jobs -y` restarted every running job in the project. Bare job actions now expand only to the jobs the bare command would act on: `start` to stopped and paused jobs, `restart` to jobs created with `--restart` or `--loop`, and `stop` / `pause` to running jobs. `compose stop jobs` and `compose pause jobs` also keep their confirmation prompt.

### v4.1.3

- **Scope `compose start jobs` (and other job actions) to the project.**
  Job actions without job names were passed straight through to `mrsm`, so `mrsm compose start jobs` started every stopped job in the root directory, not just the project's. Projects sharing a root directory then had their jobs started with the calling project's environment and config, losing their own connectors. `compose start`, `stop`, `pause`, `restart`, and `delete jobs` with no names now act only on the project's jobs, and naming a job owned by another Compose project is refused.

### v4.1.2

- **Serve already-imported plugins instantly from `from_plugin_import()`.**
  Every call built a new `Plugin`, activated its virtual environment (re-parsing its dependencies), and re-ran `import_plugins()`, which builds a `Plugin` for every installed plugin and creates resource directories along the way: about 4 ms per call, or 16 ms with thirty plugins installed. A fully-imported submodule is now returned straight from `sys.modules` (about 0.01 ms per call), and `Plugin.module` reuses an already-imported module. Reloading or unloading plugins still picks up new code.

- **Return one `None` per name when `from_plugin_import()` fails.**
  A failed submodule import returned a single `None` even when several attributes were requested, so `a, b = from_plugin_import(...)` raised a confusing unpacking error far from the cause. It now returns one `None` per requested attribute, after the existing warning and stacktrace.

- **Cut the fixed overhead of `Pipe.get_data()`.**
  `attempt_import()` activated the `mrsm` virtual environment on every call, even for modules already imported, and `get_data()` makes dozens of these calls. Loaded modules are now returned directly. `get_data()` also skips re-sorting in Pandas when the datetime column is already unique and in order (as returned by the SQL `ORDER BY`); ties and nulls are still fully sorted. A warm `get_data()` on a small SQLite pipe dropped from 24 ms to 13 ms.

- **Create one PostgreSQL unique structure for upsert pipes.**
  PostgreSQL-family connectors created a unique index and then added an equivalent unique constraint, which built a second backing index over the same columns. New upsert pipes now create the constraint only, recognize its `UQ_` backing index on later index passes, and drop either the new single structure or a legacy `IX_` + `UQ_` pair correctly.

- **Serialize first reads of shared pipe metadata.**
  Concurrent readers could observe an unfinished attribute load and cache a guessed table name, producing errors such as `relation "public.acme_clients_sites" does not exist` despite a registered `clients_sites` target. Attribute loads now serialize per pipe and mark metadata fresh only after success. Failed SQL or API reads warn and remain retryable, registered pipes with empty parameters do not cache guessed targets, and an explicit parameter refresh invalidates the target and freshness caches.

- **Record clean daemon stops as successful.**
  The daemon's own shutdown handler raises `SystemExit(0)`, but the result recorder classified it as a failure and stored a red `SystemExit: 0` traceback. Exit codes `None` and `0` now record a successful stop; nonzero exits, `KeyboardInterrupt`, and `BrokenPipeError` remain failures. A `Failed to gracefully quit` warning now includes the underlying quit reason.

- **Keep full tracebacks for failed daemon actions.**
  Non-debug daemon actions previously discarded the stack trace and suggested rerunning with `--debug`, losing the evidence needed to diagnose intermittent background failures. Daemons now log the full traceback while retaining a concise failure result; foreground non-debug errors remain concise.

### v4.1.1

- **Honor an explicitly empty routes allowlist.**
  `api:permissions:routes:allowlist: []` (the documented way to serve nothing but `/login` and plugin routes) was treated as unset (`[] or ['*']`) and silently served every core route group. An empty list now registers no core route groups; only a missing (or null) allowlist falls back to `['*']`.

- **Boot with a restricted allowlist.**
  With no authenticated core routes registered, the generated OpenAPI schema has no `components.securitySchemes`, and the startup event crashed with `KeyError: 'securitySchemes'`, a crash loop, on exactly the locked-down deployments the allowlist exists for. The schema sections are now created when absent.

### v4.1.0

- **Filter Polars DataFrames against a pipe without converting to Pandas.**
  `Pipe.filter_existing()` raised `AttributeError: 'DataFrame' object has no attribute 'empty'` when handed a `polars.DataFrame`, because the guard which detects non-DataFrame input matches on the string `'dataframe'` and a Polars frame's type name contains it. A Polars `DataFrame` or `LazyFrame` is now accepted, and the three returned frames (unseen, update, delta) are Polars frames rather than Pandas ones.

  The comparison itself also runs natively: the existing rows are read with `Pipe.get_data(as_polars=True)`, and both the delta anti-join and the unseen / update split are performed by Polars, so no frame is round-tripped through Pandas. On a 150k-row sync against SQLite this cuts `filter_existing()` from 1.49s to 0.94s. Frames which Polars cannot compare (`uuid`, `object`, and geometry columns, or pipes using `autoincrement` / `autotime`) transparently fall back to the Pandas implementation and are converted back to Polars on the way out. Where the incoming and stored frames disagree on a dtype within the same family (Pandas never downcasts, so an incoming `int64` meets Oracle's stored `int32`), both are widened to their common dtype; anything else, such as an `int` against a `float`, falls back to Pandas, which coerces mixed numerics into `numeric` values. Pandas remains the default: a Pandas frame in is still filtered by Pandas and returned as Pandas.

  ```python
  import polars as pl
  import meerschaum as mrsm

  pipe = mrsm.Pipe('demo', 'polars', instance='sql:main')
  unseen_df, update_df, delta_df = pipe.filter_existing(pl.DataFrame(docs))
  ```

- **Speed up shell autocompletion.**
  Typing a flag in the shell was laggy: `-c` (and any other incomplete flag) re-parsed the
  line through the pretty-printed error path on every keystroke, and completing a connector
  re-imported every installed plugin. `argparse` failures now raise directly instead of
  routing through `meerschaum.utils.warnings.error()` (whose Rich traceback was built and then discarded), and
  `get_data_plugins()` caches its result against the installed plugins' names. With 21
  plugins installed, a keystroke after `-c` fell from 275 ms to 8 ms.

- **Preserve dtypes when splitting new rows from updated rows.**
  `filter_existing()` separated the two with `joined_df.where(mask).dropna(how='all')`, which masks the non-matching rows to null before dropping them. That upcast integer and boolean columns to `float` or `object` on the way through, and silently discarded any row whose values were all null. Both frames are now selected with a boolean mask, which keeps the dtypes and the rows.


- **Grant admins every scope at `/login`.**
